course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Final Project I
course.description: Final Project I is a project‑based learning course in which students work in teams to initiate and design a data science and engineering project addressing a real‑world problem. Across 16 weeks, students conduct stakeholder and market analysis, perform literature reviews, and develop clear functional and non‑functional requirements to define the project scope. They build hands‑on experience by collecting, cleaning, and preprocessing data, and by developing baseline prototypes using machine learning, deep learning, NLP, or time‑series approaches. The course emphasizes analytical reasoning, technical skills, ethical awareness, and collaborative teamwork. Students communicate progress through presentations, peer reviews, and a final report and demo. Project I prepares students for Project II, where the full system will be refined, extended, and deployed.

topics.title: Topic 1: Project Orientation, Problem Scoping, Team forming
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify the scope, purpose, and expectations of the Project I course. LLO2: Form project teams and define team roles and responsibilities. LLO3: Apply basic scoping techniques to draft an initial project problem statement.

topics.title: Topic 2: Stakeholder and Market discovery
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify key stakeholders relevant to the project problem. LLO2: Analyze market needs and gaps using structured inquiry methods. LLO3: Collect preliminary stakeholder insights to refine the problem scope.

topics.title: Topic 3: Literature Review
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Search and retrieve academic sources related to the project domain. LLO2: Summarize key findings and trends from selected research papers LLO3: Compare existing solutions to determine opportunities for improvement.

topics.title: Topic 3: Literature Review
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Critically evaluate methodologies used in relevant literature. LLO2: Synthesize insights from multiple sources to justify design choices. LLO3: Present a structured literature review outline supporting the project direction.

topics.title: Topic 4: Requirements Engineering, Use Cases, Data Source Mapping
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify functional and non‑functional requirements for the proposed system. LLO2: Develop use‑case diagrams to describe user interactions with the system. LLO3: Map potential data sources relevant to the defined requirements.

topics.title: Topic 4: Requirements Engineering, Use Cases, Data Source Mapping
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Refine requirements through stakeholder feedback and feasibility analysis. LLO2: Evaluate potential data sources for accessibility and suitability. LLO3: Construct a complete requirements specification document.

topics.title: Topic 5: Ethical AI, Bias, Fairness & Data Privacy
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Apply appropriate techniques to collect raw project data. LLO2: Develop initial data-cleaning procedures for handling missing or inconsistent data. LLO3: Document the data collection workflow for reproducibility.

topics.title: Topic 6: Data Collection, Data Cleaning Pipelines
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Implement data preprocessing techniques to prepare datasets for modeling. LLO2: Adapt data pipelines to improve data quality and consistency. LLO3: Validate processed datasets through exploratory data analysis (EDA).

topics.title: Topic 6: Data Collection, Data Cleaning Pipelines
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify suitable modeling approaches for the project problem. LLO2: Apply basic implementation of selected models using appropriate tools. LLO3: Evaluate initial model performance using appropriate metrics.

topics.title: Topic 7: Modeling Approaches: ML, DL, NLP, Time Series, Graph ML
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Tune model parameters to improve baseline performance. LLO2: Compare different model families (ML vs DL vs NLP vs TS vs Graph ML). LLO3: Select the most appropriate model based on performance and project constraints.

topics.title: Topic 7: Modeling Approaches: ML, DL, NLP, Time Series, Graph ML
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Design the initial prototype integrating data pipelines and models. LLO2: Develop an evaluation strategy aligned with project objectives. LLO3: Implement prototype components for functional testing.

topics.title: Topic 8: Prototype Development & Evaluation Strategy
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Refine the prototype based on testing results and identified issues. LLO2: Apply evaluation metrics to measure prototype effectiveness. LLO3: Prepare a demonstration plan highlighting key prototype features.

topics.title: Topic 8: Prototype Development & Evaluation Strategy
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify ethical risks related to dataset bias and model fairness. LLO2: Apply ethical frameworks to evaluate the project’s AI approach. LLO3: Propose mitigation strategies to address fairness and privacy concerns.

topics.title: Topic 9: Progress Presentation & Peer Review
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Present project progress clearly and professionally to peers. LLO2: Provide constructive peer feedback based on project quality and clarity. LLO3: Reflect on received feedback to identify areas of improvement.

topics.title: Topic 9: Progress Presentation & Peer Review
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Demonstrate improved communication and presentation techniques. LLO2: Incorporate peer and instructor feedback into project refinement. LLO3: Collaborate effectively within the team to address project challenges.

topics.title: Topic 10: Submission of Final Project I Report & Demo
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Deliver a complete project report summarizing the research, design, implementation, and evaluation. LLO2: Demonstrate the final prototype through a structured presentation and live demo. LLO3: Reflect on personal and team performance throughout the project lifecycle.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Students must abide by the following policies: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
